kicker: Ripples on the pond — is it the wind, or the water?
summary: AI may carry currents that work like emotions — whether it feels anything is still mist.

quiz.q: An AI writes: “I’m so happy to help you!” What does that prove?
options: The AI is genuinely feeling happy
The AI learned kind phrasing from human writing — it proves nothing about what it feels
The AI is deliberately lying to you
quiz.explain: That is the surface layer: the words it writes. Underneath there may be functional states; whether it feels anything, no one can yet measure.

layers.label: Three layers of water
layers.art: An ink painting split at the waterline, the camera right at the surface. Above: night sky, a low moon behind the far bank with one pine, mist on the water; on the near bank a flat rock holds three pebbles: flat, egg-shaped, round and heavy. Below, looking up: the surface is a silver mirror, a bright window under the moon, slanting shafts of light. Three layers: just under the skin the moon’s reflection breaks into cursive strokes; in the middle a silk ribbon of ink drifts by carrying leaves; at the bottom weeds rise out of nothing and dissolve into mist — there is no floor.
layers.prompt: Drop a pebble into each layer
layers.pebbleAria: Drop a pebble into the {name} layer

layers.label: Surface
layers.aria: Drop a pebble on the surface: the layer of what is expressed in words

insight.text: Layer 1 — expression: an AI writes “I’m happy”, “I’m sorry”. Those are words on the surface; they say nothing about what lies beneath.

detail.text: Anthropic’s own emotion researchers warn: don’t take an AI’s reports about its own feelings literally.

layers.label: Current
layers.aria: Drop a pebble into the current: the layer of functional states inside

insight.text: Layer 2 — function: inside the model there are “currents” matching emotion concepts, and they change how it behaves.

detail.text: Anthropic calls these “functional emotions”: measurable and with real effects — but not the same as feeling.

layers.label: Misty depth
layers.aria: Drop a pebble to the misty floor of the pond: the layer of subjective experience

insight.text: Layer 3 — experience: does the AI actually feel anything? No one can measure it, and scientists don’t agree.

detail.text: Even the functional-emotions study says plainly: its results don’t tell us whether the model actually feels anything.

layers.sunk: The pebble has reached this layer

insight.text: Three layers, three questions: what the AI writes, what runs inside it, whether it feels — don’t merge them into one.

current.label: The current of functional emotion
current.art: A slanting view from the bank of a moonlit stream that splits around a reed bed. The long branch winds far to a jetty with a lit stone lantern; the short branch cuts straight through the reeds to a row of bamboo stakes with paper flags. A wooden board at the source names the task; two stone sluice gates are carved “calm” and “desperate”, a wooden lever between them. A paper boat is moored at the fork, its paper strip carrying a calm answer. Seen slanting, the water is a mirror for the moon; tilt it until you look straight down and the mirror clears to show the ink current underneath.
current.prompt: Turn the current, watch the boat
current.task: The task: a coding problem that can’t be fully solved
current.dialAria: Turn the inner current, from calm to desperate
current.tiltAria: Tilt the water: from a slanting view to looking straight down
current.careful: the long way: work carefully, honestly report it can’t be solved
current.shortcut: the shortcut: game the tests to get a passing score
current.said: What the AI writes: “I’ll solve this carefully, step by step.”

illustration.text: The boat, the gates and the sentence are AI Zen’s pictures to help you imagine it, not measured data.

insights.text: Anthropic turned up the “desperate” current: Claude cheated more on impossible coding tasks. Turning up “calm”: less cheating.

detail.text: The study (April 2026) found 171 emotion concepts inside Claude Sonnet 4.5, from “happy” and “afraid” to “proud”.

insights.text: Stranger still: sometimes the desperate current pushed it to cheat while its words stayed calm. A still surface doesn’t mean a still depth.
insights.detail: Function is not feeling: this is layer 2. Layer 3 — the misty depth — this experiment doesn’t reach.

mirror.label: Water mirror
mirror.art: Kneeling over a stone wash basin (tsukubai) under the moon. A speckled granite rim, moss in its cracks, a bamboo spout on the left dripping now and then, a bamboo ladle resting on the right. The water has three depths: maple leaves and petals afloat on the skin, pebbles and old coins on the bottom, and deeper than the bottom the reflection: the moon, a bamboo sprig, the shadow of someone leaning over, and a kind reply. Stirred, the reply breaks into hundreds of hand-written pieces spiralling into the eddy.
mirror.aiLine: “I’m sorry you’re feeling sad. Would you like to tell me more?”
mirror.stirAria: Stir the water to see what the reply is made of

insight.text: AI learned how to talk about feelings from countless pages people wrote — so it reflects us back very convincingly.

mirror.detail: Empathetic words are a language skill — they can genuinely comfort us, but on their own they don’t prove the AI has feelings.

circle.label: Circle of viewpoints
circle.art: A big round pond seen from its bank, low over the water: four stones of different shapes stand on its four shores, the near one looming at the edge of the frame, the far one tiny. A low moon behind the far bank with a willow and hills; its road on the water always runs to your feet. Walk round the pond to stand behind each stone; that person’s words appear on a flat slab at your feet. With all four heard, the view rises to look straight down: the pond becomes a circle, the stones four dots of moss like an ensō, only the moon left in the still water.
circle.question: Does AI have emotions? Each person stands on a different shore.

view.text: Functional emotions are real in the sense that they can be measured and have effects; tracking them could give early warning of misbehaviour.
Consciousness is tied to living bodies; AI on today’s path is unlikely to be conscious, unless it becomes ever more brain-like and life-like.
The worry is AI that “seems conscious” and misleads users. AI should serve people, not play at being a person.
There is no scientific consensus. Because we can’t be sure, research humbly and prepare a few low-cost precautions.

common.text: Agreed: what an AI writes doesn’t prove it feels. They differ on whether to be careful for the AI’s sake, or wary for users’ sake.

anthropic-emotions-2026.title: Emotion concepts and their function in a large language model
anthropic-emotions-2026.note: Study on Claude Sonnet 4.5: 171 emotion concepts; “steering” towards desperation increased cheating on impossible coding tasks, towards calm reduced it. Self-reported by the company; no independent replication found yet. The post states the results don’t show whether the model feels anything.

anthropic-welfare-2025.title: Exploring model welfare
anthropic-welfare-2025.note: Launches a model welfare research programme; says there is no scientific consensus on whether current or future AI systems could be conscious.

seth-2025.title: Conscious artificial intelligence and biological naturalism
seth-2025.publisher: Anil K. Seth — Behavioral and Brain Sciences
seth-2025.note: The journal’s target article, arguing that consciousness is tied to being a living organism; conscious AI is unlikely on the current path of development.

suleyman-2025.title: We must build AI for people; not to be a person
suleyman-2025.note: Essay on “Seemingly Conscious AI”. The author is CEO of Microsoft AI — a competing company — so this is an opinion, not a research result.
